title: Fix X11 window positioning for tiling WM

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #105419, 
- Closes #118553, 
- Closes #113118.

## Additional information

In tiling window managers (for example Awesome WM), Godot windows are created with the correct centered position, but are immediately moved by the window manager to another place (in my case, it is one of the four corners of the screen).

When this was discussed — other users do not see this on ordinary window managers in X11. The problem will become clear below.

### First, I used `xev -root`:
<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>

```text
CreateNotify event, serial 21, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    parent 0x3d7, window 0x4200002, (384,216), width 1152, height 648
    border_width 0, override NO

CreateNotify event, serial 21, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    parent 0x3d7, window 0x4257aa, (384,216), width 1152, height 648
    border_width 0, override YES

ReparentNotify event, serial 21, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    event 0x3d7, window 0x4200002, parent 0x4257aa,
    (0,0), override NO

ConfigureNotify event, serial 21, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    event 0x3d7, window 0x4257aa, (384,216), width 1152, height 648,
    border_width 0, above 0x0, override YES

PropertyNotify event, serial 21, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x193 (_NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING), time 44009724, state PropertyNewValue

PropertyNotify event, serial 21, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x193 (_NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING), time 44009724, state PropertyNewValue

PropertyNotify event, serial 21, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x192 (_NET_CLIENT_LIST), time 44009724, state PropertyNewValue

PropertyNotify event, serial 21, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x15a (_NET_CURRENT_DESKTOP), time 44009725, state PropertyNewValue

PropertyNotify event, serial 22, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x193 (_NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING), time 44009732, state PropertyNewValue

PropertyNotify event, serial 22, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x193 (_NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING), time 44009732, state PropertyNewValue

PropertyNotify event, serial 22, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x159 (_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW), time 44009732, state PropertyNewValue

PropertyNotify event, serial 22, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x15a (_NET_CURRENT_DESKTOP), time 44009733, state PropertyNewValue

PropertyNotify event, serial 22, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x159 (_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW), time 44009733, state PropertyNewValue

PropertyNotify event, serial 22, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    atom 0x15a (_NET_CURRENT_DESKTOP), time 44009733, state PropertyNewValue

ConfigureNotify event, serial 22, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    event 0x3d7, window 0x4257aa, (0,432), width 1152, height 648,
    border_width 0, above 0x0, override YES

MapNotify event, serial 22, synthetic NO, window 0x3d7,
    event 0x3d7, window 0x4257aa, override YES
```

</details>

Screen resolution: 1920×1080. Godot creates a 1152×648 window, which should be located in the center of the screen at coordinates (384, 216).

Sequence of events:

1. **CreateNotify:**
    Godot creates the client window with the correct position (384,216).
2. **ReparentNotify:**
    WM places the window inside its frame.
3. **Problem:**
    The second ConfigureNotify.
    WM forcibly moves the window to (0,432) (the bottom-left corner) immediately before displaying it.
4. **MapNotify:**
    The window appears already in the wrong position.

### Debugging via `xprop | grep -E "WM_CLASS|WM_WINDOW_TYPE|WM_NAME"`:
```text
_NET_WM_NAME(UTF8_STRING) = "test (DEBUG)"
_NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE(ATOM) = _NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE_NORMAL
WM_CLASS(STRING) = "Godot_Engine", "test"
WM_NAME(STRING) = "test (DEBUG)"
```

Since `WM_WINDOW_TYPE` has the value `NORMAL`, the tiling WM treats the window as a normal managed client that needs to be placed in its layout, unlike floating dialog windows. More on this below.

### Unsuccessful alternative solutions

1. **Adding USPosition:**

      Godot in display_server_x11.cpp uses:
      ```
      PPosition | PSize
      ```
      There was an attempt to modify `_update_size_hints():`
      ```
      xsh->flags |= USPosition | PSize | PWinGravity;
      ```
      in order to inform the WM that the window position is set by the user.

      This did not help. WMs like Awesome still apply their own rules (awful.placement) and ignore this hint.

2. **Changing Gravity:**

      An attempt to replace `StaticGravity` with `NorthWestGravity` also did not help.

3. **Changing the window type:**

      In general, this started with 4.5-4.6 when many windows were moved out of the main window and became `popup`.

      I found that PR #55415 proposed using `_NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE_DIALOG`.

      This disables tiling behavior and fixes the problem for child windows.

      However, this type cannot be used for the main game or editor window.

      Although this is a good solution for internal dialog windows, which also fixes this PR but in a different way. In general, everything came together into a single picture, and I can point out other issues that could potentially be closed and where I encountered this: #118553 and #113118.

### Solution

Since the WM ignores X11 hints and overwrites the initial coordinates, the only way to guarantee the position is to override the WM action after it has applied its layout.

The PR implements a forced position change through `XConfigureWindow(CWX|CWY)`.

**Algorithm:**
- The requested window position is stored.
- A wait is performed after `XMapWindow` and `XSync`.
- After a small delay (~50 ms), `XConfigureWindow` is called.

**Note:**

Since the position is corrected only after the WM has already placed the window, a visual "jump" appears:
- the window first appears in the corner;
- then it is instantly moved to the center.

On larger windows this is not very noticeable, but the method reliably sets the correct position. In general, this looks like a normal practice for window loading. At least on Windows this has been the case from XP until now, when a window appears from the top-left corner and then moves to the center.

A similar error correction logic was already discussed in #75709. Although my solution does not have a negative impact on regular stacking WMs. That is, in the normal case and on many WMs, the jump should not occur due to the check.

This is precisely why it solves most of the mentioned problems. However, regarding #55415, I would implement it on top of all this, although, as I said, this PR solves it in a different way.
